newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian spies woo foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Russian spies woo foreign investors.

text.p: Russia's spies, long trained to hound capitalists, are now doing a good job at wooing them, the head of the Federal Security Service said on Wednesday.

FSB chief Nikolai Kovalyov told Itar-Tass news agency that his agents had already helped to attract a multi-million dollar credit to the country and were now helping to bring in new multi-billion dollar investments.

"We basically attract investment under FSB guarantees," said Kovalyov, explaining that the special services offer Western investors working in goverment programmes "information and physical security".
Information security involves finding them reliable partners, while physical security is only offered in extraordinary circumstances, Tass said.
"We don't have extensive means for this. But if a project merits it, we provide such security," Kovalyov said, without saying which projects the agency was involved in.
Kovalyov, appointed last July, has said he favours non-traditional work methods. He first raised the idea of such an initiative at last year's World Economic Forum in Davos, Tass said.
"After this there were a flood of calls. Now the service plays a modest part in the country's economic development," the agency quoted Kovalyov as saying.
The FSB is the successor to the dreaded former Soviet KGB.
